html:
The Tirukkural, or Kural, is a Tamil book of 1,330 couplets on how to live, credited to the poet Thiruvalluvar. Its date is disputed. Many scholars place it around 450 to 500 CE; Tamil tradition puts it centuries earlier.

Each couplet has just seven words, four in the first line and three in the second. The couplets are grouped in tens under 133 headings and three parts:

  • virtue: the home, kindness, truth, not killing, not eating meat;
  • wealth: the king, ministers, spies, friendship, farming;
  • love: the secret meetings of lovers, and married life.

The book names no god, sect or caste, and Hindus, Jains, Buddhists and Christians have each claimed its author. Almost nothing is known about him. Tradition makes him a weaver of Mylapore, now part of Chennai.

It came after Sangam literature and is the most quoted book in Tamil. A missionary put part of it into Latin in 1730, and it has since been translated into more than forty languages. Leo Tolstoy quoted its verses on not returning evil in a 1908 letter that Gandhi read. A 41-metre statue of the poet stands in the sea at Kanyakumari.
sum: The Tirukkural, or Kural, is a Tamil book of 1,330 couplets on how to live, credited to the poet Thiruvalluvar. Its date is disputed. Many scholars place it around 450 to 500 CE; Tamil tradition puts it centuries earlier.
